original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.

actual_scope: Integrate PR1029 sparse exact state evaluation with PR662 gate tables into both Clifford-using stages of the complete warp-aware PR2751 T74 native replay. Benchmark complete five-stage runs against the unchanged driver.
scope_change_reason: The earlier U8 fast runners omit the present T74 independent warp-recipe stage. This scope keeps that stage and all other native controls.
task_classification: Explicit engineering override after comparing three narrow candidates; retained assignment seed2, no new random novelty claim.
candidate_tasks: Further source aliases: limited fixed-word headroom after PR2751.
Common-prefix mutation replay: higher coverage/invalidation risk.
Complete T74 sparse native integration: measured phase lowering bottleneck, chosen.
bottleneck_link: Reducing the cost of fresh exact native admission lets changed-word candidates and independent reviewers iterate sooner.
stop_rule: One source snapshot and two PR2751 provider words; three alternating paired base benchmarks, complete extra replay, output equivalence and boundary controls. No wider algorithmic search.
evidence: Three alternating paired complete base native runs: median306.7496s reference versus85.8840s sparse (3.57167x).
